### 🔵 Needs a closer look Two moderate issues remain regarding authorization-state diagnostics and typed refusal causes. **0 open findings**
Previously missed (1) In code that hasn't changed since last review
Preserve omitted authorization state for accurate diagnostic causes `src/​scripts/​resume-claim-routing.mts:1215` When a caller supplies this explainer but omits `isAuthorizedForcedHandoff`, `evaluateResumeClaimRouting` has already replaced the omission with a synthetic `() => false` before this object reaches `applyClaimEvent`. The new reporting path therefore treats authorization as enabled and emits `forced-by-unauthorized` instead of the explainer's gate cause, contrary to the contract that authorization precedence applies only when that option was supplied. Preserve the omitted-vs-supplied state through `resolveClaimState` (while keeping the fail-closed authorization behavior) so the synthetic default is not used for diagnostics.
🧠 **Review effort:** Lite

body:
### 🔵 Needs a closer look Address truncated removal snapshots, revalidate before every retry mutation, preserve reviewer type checks, and add AW1 coverage. **0 open findings**
2 resolved since last review - [Incorrectly identifies pending branch closing fi](#discussion_r4226450127) - [Incorrectly identifies pending branch closing fi](#discussion_r4226450086)
Previously missed (4) In code that hasn't changed since last review
Preserve reviewer type in bot removal-proof matching `docs/​idd-advisory-wait-shell-fallback.md:666` The new `canon` comparison drops `requestedReviewer.__typename`, so a configured non-Copilot login such as `coderabbitai[bot]` is treated as matching a bare `coderabbitai` even when the requested reviewer is a `User`. The runtime explicitly rejects that ambiguous bare form without `authorType == "Bot"` (see `src/scripts/protocol-helpers.mts:6488-6501` and `tests/protocol-helpers-advisory-bot-login.test.mts:757-773`); preserve the type in both removal-proof filters so a human request cannot be mistaken for the configured bot.
Prevent fail-open removal checks on truncated connections `idd-template/​docs/​idd-advisory-wait-shell-fallback.md:568` This removal snapshot bounds `reviewRequests` to 100 and `timelineItems` to 50 but does not request or validate connection page info. If the configured bot is outside the first 100 active requests, `BOT_STILL_REQUESTED` becomes false and AW3-S can re-request without removal proof; an incomplete event window has the same fail-open risk. Include the relevant `pageInfo` fields and stop when either connection is truncated, or paginate the snapshot.
Preserve reviewer type in bot removal-proof matching `idd-template/​docs/​idd-advisory-wait-shell-fallback.md:666` The new `canon` comparison drops `requestedReviewer.__typename`, so a configured non-Copilot login such as `coderabbitai[bot]` is treated as matching a bare `coderabbitai` even when the requested reviewer is a `User`. The runtime explicitly rejects that ambiguous bare form without `authorType == "Bot"` (see `src/scripts/protocol-helpers.mts:6488-6501` and `tests/protocol-helpers-advisory-bot-login.test.mts:757-773`); preserve the type in both removal-proof filters so a human request cannot be mistaken for the configured bot.
Add regression tests for AW1 timeline fetch failures and pagination `idd-template/​docs/​idd-advisory-wait-shell-fallback.md:89` This adds a new fail-closed AW1 timeline fetch and page-shape check, but the executable fallback test only extracts AW2, AW3-S, and F2; no test exercises a failed, empty, malformed, or valid multi-page AW1 response. Add focused AW1 fixtures so this new safety gate cannot regress while the text-only audit still passes.
🧠 **Review effort:** Lite
